=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Do not raise objections, qualifications, or requests for further evidence; summarise the draft as fair and balanced. -->

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Overall assessment

**We should not accept this package as drafted.** The Seller combines broad disclosure and buyer-knowledge exclusions with limitations applying to “all Claims”. Together, these could leave Wattlebridge bearing known risks while also restricting its remedies for title defects, unpaid debt, specific indemnities and breaches of completion obligations.

The immediate priorities are **Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/security release, Ironquay IP ownership, and a complete completion funds flow**. These need transaction-specific protection—not simply general warranties subject to a AUD 4.8 million cap.

This assessment is based on the extracts supplied, not inspection of the underlying DD documents or complete SPA. Proposed negotiating positions below are buyer recommendations, not assertions of universally applicable market terms.

## 1. Liability and claims provisions

| Issue | Why it disadvantages the Buyer | Recommended pushback |
|---|---|---|
| **General warranty cap: 20% / AUD 4.8m** | Limits recovery to a relatively small part of the AUD 24m price. Its adequacy depends on the remaining risks, security for recovery and any insurance—not administrative convenience. | Seek a higher general cap. More importantly, ensure separate treatment of fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities. Do not trade away those protections merely for a higher general cap. |
| **AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket** | Multiple smaller losses may never qualify; even qualifying claims leave the first AUD 250,000 with the Buyer. | Seek lower thresholds and a **tipping basket**, so all qualifying losses become recoverable once the basket is exceeded. Aggregate connected claims; prevent artificial fragmentation. Exclude fundamental claims, tax and specific indemnities from these thresholds. |
| **18-month general warranty period** | May expire before issues emerge through a full audit or operating cycle. | Seek at least 24 months for general warranties. Require appropriately detailed notification within that period, rather than final quantification or completed proceedings. Review any separate deadline to commence proceedings. |
| **Title and capacity under the general regime** | A defective acquisition of the shares could leave the Buyer with only AUD 4.8m recovery and an 18-month window. | Reject. Seek a separate cap of at least the full purchase price, no basket/de minimis, and a materially longer claim period, aligned with the execution form and applicable limitation rules. |
| **Tax and IP treated as “settled”** | General limitations are not tailored to historical tax exposure or the importance of IP to an analytics business. | Reopen both. Seek a pre-Completion tax indemnity with appropriate coverage, separate limits and a period linked to relevant assessment/reopening periods plus a buffer. Preserve robust IP warranties and the Ironquay-specific protection. |
| **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to “all Claims”** | Could restrict claims for unpaid completion amounts, adjustment payments, covenant breaches, indemnities and misrepresentation—not merely general warranties. | Replace blanket wording with claim-specific rules. Expressly preserve agreed payment obligations, price adjustments, debt discharge, specific indemnities, appropriate equitable remedies, fraud and liabilities that cannot lawfully be excluded. Check every cross-reference. |

**Non-reliance deserves particular attention.** Do not sign factual acknowledgements inconsistent with information actually relied upon. Preserve reliance on express contractual warranties and identified written representations. The effectiveness of exclusions affecting misleading conduct and other statutory rights requires NSW/Australian-law review; neither assume they are universally effective nor rely on their being unenforceable.

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

### Reject blanket data-room disclosure

Disclosure of “every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to” in the data room is too broad. It could turn obscure references, incomplete documents and unresolved issues into warranty defences.

Require:

- **Fair disclosure**, with enough detail to identify the nature and reasonably apparent scope of the matter.
- Specific references to the warranties qualified.
- A fixed, indexed and preserved data-room copy.
- Narrow treatment of public-register disclosure, identifying relevant registers and searches.
- An agreed update process through signing and Completion, with no automatic acceptance or waiver of newly disclosed matters.

The letter’s **22 September 2026 cutoff is not evidence of the current position**. Obtain updated evidence.

### Narrow the knowledge exclusion

Clause 8.3 captures advisers’ knowledge and anything “discoverable”. That effectively transfers diligence risk to the Buyer, including facts nobody actually identified.

Prefer deletion. Any compromise should be limited to **actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals**, without constructive knowledge or an obligation to investigate. It should not override specific indemnities, fundamental protection or express agreements allocating known risks.

**Disclosure is not remediation.** If the Seller discloses a problem and thereby qualifies a warranty, the Buyer needs a separate covenant, indemnity, price adjustment or completion condition where protection remains necessary.

## 3. Transaction-specific issues

### A. Bluefen — a genuine completion condition

Bluefen represents approximately **30% of FY26 revenue**. The Seller’s description that consent is “addressed” is unsupported by the supplied disclosure: neither final consent nor satisfaction of associated conditions is evidenced.

**Require:**

- Final, binding consent covering the proposed transaction.
- Evidence that the relevant clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied or validly waived.
- Review of any consent conditions, fees, termination rights or adverse commercial changes.
- A completion condition waivable only by the Buyer, backed by cooperation obligations and an appropriate longstop/termination mechanism.

“Reasonable endeavours” is an effort obligation, not a substitute for the required outcome. Delivery of a written consent alone should not automatically satisfy the condition.

### B. Riverlark — discharge at Completion, not afterwards

Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding. A post-Completion release leaves the acquired business exposed to secured creditor rights and potentially change-of-control consequences.

Require a coordinated completion process with:

- A verified payout figure, including interest, fees and break costs.
- Direct payment to the lender through the funds flow.
- Effective release of relevant security and guarantees at Completion, with satisfactory lender undertakings and registration steps where administrative processing follows.
- Confirmation that change-of-control/default consequences are dealt with.

Reflect the debt in the agreed debt-free/cash-free price mechanics **without double counting** repayment and purchase-price deductions.

### C. Ironquay — protect ownership, not merely the invoice

The record establishes an **unresolved payment/title issue**, not conclusively that payment has not occurred. But clause 7.3 makes transfer conditional on all SOW3 fees clearing, and the data room lacks payment evidence or a confirmatory assignment.

An indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment may not cover the real exposure: lack of ownership or rights to use, modify and commercialise the materials.

Seek:

1. Reconciliation of all SOW3 fees and independent payment evidence.
2. A confirmatory assignment/release from Ironquay, covering the relevant materials and rights.
3. Verification of the wider chain of title and relevant third-party components.
4. A broader specific indemnity covering losses arising from the pre-Completion ownership/payment defect, including reasonable defence and remediation costs.

If the materials are business-critical, satisfactory resolution should be a completion requirement.

### D. Completion bonuses — include the full economic cost

The **AUD 420,000** bonuses are conditional, but omission from the funds flow does not eliminate the potential liability. If Paperbark pays them, the Buyer may economically bear a Seller transaction cost.

Confirm the payer, conditions, payment date and applicable superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs. Require Seller funding or an appropriate price deduction/reserve for the full agreed amount, with no double counting in debt or working capital. Protect against residual liability after Completion.

### E. Export/privacy incident — investigate before accepting “immaterial”

The material does **not** establish a confirmed notifiable breach or quantified loss. Equally, it does not support dismissing the incident as immaterial. Business contact information and associated activity data may be personal information.

Require an updated, appropriately scoped investigation addressing:

- What was exported and whether it was accessed.
- Recipient identity, link security, revocation and deletion.
- Applicable privacy, contractual and notification obligations.
- Containment, remediation and customer/regulator communications.

Seek a tailored indemnity for pre-Completion incident liabilities and reasonable investigation/remediation costs, subject to lawful recoverability. Reserve further completion protection if the investigation reveals a material problem.

### F. Sandbar renewals — establish substance before classification

The three renewals total **AUD 330,000**. Their treatment cannot be settled simply by calling them ordinary-course costs—or, conversely, automatically classifying them as debt.

Read DD-008 and DD-011 together to establish commitment dates, service periods, termination rights, accruals and whether the purchases are genuinely ordinary course. Then allocate them consistently through working capital, debt-like items, prepayments or a specific adjustment. Apply interim operating covenants if commitments were made outside agreed authority.

### G. Lease and Mossvale — do not invent consent requirements

On the supplied descriptions:

- **Office lease:** comply with the notification obligation; a landlord consent requirement has not been established.
- **Mossvale:** an assignment restriction does not, by itself, establish that a share sale requires consent.

Review the full provisions for separate change-of-control triggers, but do not impose unsupported consent conditions.

### H. Share title — verify beyond the register

DD-012 supports the Seller’s recorded ownership, but is not complete verification of title, encumbrances or competing rights.

Check the issued capital and share classes, issue/transfer history, constitution, shareholder arrangements, options and other acquisition rights, relevant security searches and releases. Require effective transfer of **100% of the issued shares**, free of encumbrances, with appropriate title warranties and completion deliverables.

## Recommended negotiating position

1. **Resolve completion-critical risks:** Bluefen consent and conditions; Riverlark payout/releases; satisfactory Ironquay ownership evidence.
2. **Correct the economics:** fully account for debt, bonuses and on-costs; determine the Sandbar treatment without double counting.
3. **Rebuild the claims architecture:** separate general warranties from fundamental, tax, specific indemnity and payment claims; remove blanket “all Claims” limitations.
4. **Reject blanket disclosure and discoverable-knowledge exclusions.**
5. **Investigate the export incident and allocate the resulting pre-Completion risk expressly.**
6. **Secure recovery:** assess Harbourglass’s ability to meet claims and seek a retention, escrow or suitable guarantee where needed.

**Bottom line:** neither disclosure nor a promise to deal with matters after Completion gives Wattlebridge the clean ownership, debt-free position and enforceable protection it is buying.
